messages:
alex: Quick follow-up on the Dedicated GPU orchestration RFC 
I want to propose a lightweight 'lease-proxy' pattern that splits fast soft prewarm leases from the strong allocation lease. Goal: cut cold-start tail without over-committing billing or eviction surface.

maria: OK, outline invariants and failure modes. How do we avoid double-counting headroom or accidental over-provisioning?

alex: Invariants: 1) soft_lease = ephemeral, not billed to tenant, can be revoked any time; holds weights/KV cache + warm runtime state. 2) promotion -> strong_lease when headroom token available; strong_lease is the billing unit and maps to a GPU slot. 3) only one strong_lease per tenant slot; soft leases can be shared across compatible model families. 4) soft leases have TTLs and LRU eviction.

jonathan: Tradeoffs: sharing soft leases across tenants reduces cold-starts but complicates eviction and security isolation. Promotion must be cheap (<200ms P95 target). Also need decision logic: when to promote vs serve degraded/fallback model.

riley: Telemetry requirements: emit soft_lease_acquire, soft_lease_release, soft_lease_promote, promote_latency_ms, promote_failures, promote_rate. Tag events with tenant_id, pool, model_family, and probe_id. We'll use that for SLA and tuning.

maria: Billing: only bill on promotion (creation of strong_lease and GPU attach). Add audit entries: promotion_request_id, actor, source_ip, and final decision. This satisfies finance and compliance.

alex: Admission control idea: token-bucket per pool + per-tenant rate limiter to avoid promotion stampedes. Policy on promote failure: a) queued retry with exponential backoff, b) immediate fallback to hosted/cheaper model, c) degrade response with warning header. Make this tenant-configurable and default to queued retry for PLG and fallback for enterprise.

jonathan: Operator boundary question: where does the proxy live? Options: control-plane centralized service vs per-cluster operator-local sidecar. Centralized gives global headroom visibility and simpler matching; local reduces cross-region RTT and blast radius. I lean control-plane with replicated pods and local caches.

alex: Implementation sketch: proxy exposes a Promote API: POST /promote {tenant, model, soft_lease_id, request_id}. Fast path: check local cache of headroom tokens, issue promote intent -> controller creates StrongLease CRD. Use optimistic fast-fail if headroom not available. Soft leases annotated on nodes via softLease annotation.

jonathan: Rough config example:
```
leaseProxy:
  mode: control-plane
  promoteRatePerTenant: "2/s"
  promoteBurst: 4
  sharedSoftPoolFamilies: ["llama-2-13b","redwood-verified-13b"]
  billingOnPromote: "true"
```

riley: Tests: synthetic burst test with 500 tenants, 5% concurrent promotes; assert promote latency <200ms P95 and promote_fail_rate <0.5%. Add chaos tests: leader failover, network partition, controller restart, and ensure no leaked strong leases.

maria: Rollout plan: feature-flag behind org opt-in. Start with one region, canary to 1% tenants, validate telemetry for 48h, then expand. Provide toggle to switch proxy mode control-plane vs local sidecar for A/B.

alex: Security notes: soft leases must not expose tenant secrets. Ensure soft_lease state contains only model weights/cache references, no plaintext prompts or secrets. Promotion must validate ACLs and KMS tokens before attaching GPU.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout triggered for lease-proxy v0.1 to cluster-delta :rocket:

alex: Next step: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams, state machine for acquire/promote/evict, and CRD schema. Who wants to own what?

jonathan: I'll own the StrongLease CRD + controller integration and API design.

riley: I'll own telemetry, alerts, and the synthetic test harness.

maria: I'll own billing hooks, audit schema, and rollout checklist.

alex: Perfect. I'll assemble the follow-up doc and ping eng-sre + product for feedback. :thumbsup:
